assignments.text:
We mention this fact rather as a contribution to the
history of those phenomena of the human mind, which have as yet escaped
the metaphysician, than as an actual circumstance in the life of Miss
Marjoribanks. She was a woman of genius, and he only a very simple,
unlucky fellow; and yet a sensation of comfort came to Lucilla's heart
when she said "Poor Tom!"
assignments.summary: The narrator remarks that this psychological phenomenon—genius finding comfort in simple faith—is remarkable and deserves attention.
assignments.best_quote: She was a woman of genius, and he only a very simple, unlucky fellow; and yet a sensation of comfort came to Lucilla's heart when she said 'Poor Tom!'

assignments.text:
To vanquish the Archdeacon, to pluck out from the darkness,
and rehabilitate and set at his ease the mysterious adventurer, whom, to
be sure,  she could not say she knew —for Lucilla was very careful,
even in her own thoughts, not to commit herself on this subject—and to
finish off by a glorious and triumphant marriage—not her own, it is
true, but of her making, which was more to the purpose—such was the
programme she made out for herself with the speed of lightning, the
moment she had laid hold of the clue which guided or seemed to guide her
through the labyrinth.
assignments.summary: Lucilla immediately conceives an ambitious three-fold plan: overcoming the Archdeacon's influence, redeeming Kavan, and orchestrating a triumphant reconciliation.

assignments.text:
But this news was naturally much more serious to Miss Marjoribanks when
she got upstairs, and had time to think of it. She would not have been
human if she had heard without emotion of the return of the man whom she
had once dreamed of as member for Carlingford, with the addition of
other dreams which had not been altogether without their sweetness.
assignments.summary: Lucilla recognizes that Mr Cavendish's return stirs emotions she thought past—he had been her dream candidate and romantic interest.
assignments.best_quote: She would not have been human if she had heard without emotion of the return of the man whom she had once dreamed of as member for Carlingford, with the addition of other dreams which had not been altogether without their sweetness.

assignments.text:
"My dear Barbara," she said, putting her hands on the singer's shoulders
as she finished her strain, "that is enough for to-night. Mr Cavendish
will take you downstairs and get you a cup of tea; for you know there is
no room to-night to serve it upstairs." Thus Miss Marjoribanks proved
herself capable of preferring her great work to her personal sentiments,
which is generally considered next to impossible for a woman.
assignments.summary: Lucilla firmly stops Barbara's singing, sending her downstairs with Mr Cavendish for tea, thereby proving herself capable of preferring her great work to personal sentiments.
assignments.best_quote: "My dear Barbara, that is enough for to-night. Mr Cavendish will take you downstairs and get you a cup of tea; for you know there is no room to-night to serve it upstairs."

assignments.text:
Her mother, too, had
possessed this dangerous faculty of tears; and it was not wonderful if
the sober-minded Doctor, roused for the first time to consider his
little girl as a creature possessed of individual character, should
recognise, with a thrill of dismay, the appearance of the same qualities
which had wearied his life out, and brought his youthful affections to
an untimely end.
assignments.summary: Dr Marjoribanks is horrified to recognize in Lucilla the emotional volatility that exhausted and alienated him from her mother.

assignments.text:
"You must come yourself this evening, you dear old Rose," said Lucilla. "You know I always was fond of you. Oh, yes, I know you can't sing like
Barbara. But the Archdeacon is coming, who understands about art; and if
you would like to bring your design——My principle has always been,
that there should be a little of everything in society," said Miss
Marjoribanks.
assignments.summary: Lucilla invites Rose to Thursday evening, emphasizing the Archdeacon's appreciation for art and Rose's role in exemplifying her principle of variety in society.
assignments.best_quote: You must come yourself this evening, you dear old Rose. You know I always was fond of you. Oh, yes, I know you can't sing like Barbara. But the Archdeacon is coming, who understands about art; and if you would like to bring your design——My principle has always been, that there should be a little of everything in society

assignments.text:
"Thank you for coming with me so far," said Lucilla, holding out her
hand. "I suppose I must not ask you to come in, though papa would be
delighted to see you. I am afraid you are very angry with me," Miss
Marjoribanks added, with a touch of pathos; "but you may be sure I would
always stand by  you ; and I said it because I thought it was for the
best."
assignments.summary: Lucilla bids Mr Cavendish good-night with touching assertion that she will always stand by him and that her advice was meant for his good.
assignments.best_quote: I suppose I must not ask you to come in, though papa would be delighted to see you. I am afraid you are very angry with me; but you may be sure I would always stand by you.

assignments.text:
"I am afraid I have taken your seat, papa,"
said Miss Marjoribanks, with ingenuous sweetness. "But then I should
have had to move the urn, and all the things, and I thought you would
not mind." The Doctor said nothing but "Humph!" and even that in an
undertone; but he became aware all the same that he had abdicated,
without knowing it, and that the reins of state had been smilingly
withdrawn from his unconscious hands.
assignments.summary: Lucilla apologizes sweetly, claiming she simply wanted to spare him the trouble of moving the urn; the Doctor utters only "Humph!" but understands he has surrendered power.
assignments.best_quote: he became aware all the same that he had abdicated, without knowing it, and that the reins of state had been smilingly withdrawn from his unconscious hands

assignments.text:
It was to be Tom after all—after all the
archdeacons, doctors, generals, members of Parliament—after the ten
years and more in which she had not gone off—after the poor old
Doctor's grudge against the nephew whom he did not wish to inherit his
wealth, and Aunt Jemima's quiet wiles, and attempt to disappoint her
boy.
assignments.summary: The narrator catalogues the many suitors and obstacles Tom has overcome to finally win Lucilla.
assignments.best_quote: after all the archdeacons, doctors, generals, members of Parliament—after the ten years and more in which she had not gone off

assignments.text:
This little calculation, which a timid young woman would have taken care
to do by herself, Lucilla did publicly, with her usual discrimination. The Doctor, who had looked a little grim at first, could not but laugh
when he saw the sober look of care and thought with which Miss
Marjoribanks examined her capabilities in the glass. It was not so much
the action itself that amused her father, as the consummate ability of
the young revolutionary.
assignments.summary: The Doctor is amused by Lucilla's serious self-examination, recognizing her ability to turn a self-interested act into something admirable.
assignments.best_quote: The Doctor, who had looked a little grim at first, could not but laugh when he saw the sober look of care and thought with which Miss Marjoribanks examined her capabilities in the glass. It was not so much the action itself that amused her father, as the consummate ability of the young revolutionary.

assignments.text:
Fate and honest love had been waiting all the time till their
moment came; and now it was not even necessary to say anything about it. The fact was so clear that it did not require stating. It was to be Tom
after all.
assignments.summary: Fate and honest love have prevailed; Lucilla and Tom's outcome is now clear without need for further statement.
assignments.best_quote: It was to be Tom after all.

assignments.text:
With every step
that she took, Miss Marjoribanks became more and more herself. As we
have already said, it was a grand and inspiring sight; but then, to be
sure, as in the former case, her affections, fortunately, were not
engaged. She was not in love with the Archdeacon, any more than she had
been in love with Mr Cavendish;—though it is true, love is not
everything.
assignments.summary: The narrator clarifies that Lucilla's distress stems not from lost love but from bruised pride and wounded ambition.
assignments.best_quote: She was not in love with the Archdeacon, any more than she had been in love with Mr Cavendish;—though it is true, love is not everything.

assignments.text:
"Don't tell us what marks he has on his face," said Lucilla. "I know
that I shall think every man who is dark, and has good features, and is
six feet, must be him. I wonder if it could be my cousin Tom;  he  has a
little mark on his face—and it would be just like his dreadful luck,
poor fellow.
assignments.summary: Lucilla cries out and invokes her cousin Tom as the likely candidate, joking about his bad luck while unconsciously revealing her actual suspicions.
assignments.best_quote: I wonder if it could be my cousin Tom; he has a little mark on his face—and it would be just like his dreadful luck, poor fellow.

assignments.text:
But though Lucilla was satisfied with the
events of the evening, it would be vain to deny that there were
perturbations in her mind as she laid her head upon her maiden pillow. She said to herself again with profounder fervour, that fortunately her
affections had not been engaged; but there were more things than
affections to be taken into consideration.
assignments.summary: Though Lucilla is satisfied, anxiety persists as she lies in bed, preoccupied with the mystery of the impostor and her unengaged affections.
assignments.best_quote: But though Lucilla was satisfied with the events of the evening, it would be vain to deny that there were perturbations in her mind as she laid her head upon her maiden pillow.

assignments.text:
"Perhaps I may marry some time," said Miss Marjoribanks, with composure;
"it would be foolish, you know, to make any engagements; but that will
depend greatly upon how you behave, and how Carlingford behaves, papa. I give myself ten years here, if you should be very good. By twenty-nine
I shall be going off a little, and perhaps it may be tiring, for
anything I can tell.
assignments.summary: Lucilla calmly announces that marriage depends on her father's and Carlingford's behavior, and that she gives herself ten years to accomplish her objectives before potentially seeking marriage.
assignments.best_quote: I give myself ten years here, if you should be very good. By twenty-nine I shall be going off a little, and perhaps it may be tiring, for anything I can tell.

assignments.text:
And it was thus that Lucilla made her first bold step out
of the limits of Grange Lane for the good of society, and secured at
once several important personal advantages, and the great charm of those
Thursday evenings which made so entire a revolution in the taste and
ideas of Carlingford.
assignments.summary: Through this encounter with Miss Lake, Lucilla takes her first major step beyond her home, initiating the Thursday evenings that will transform Carlingford society.
assignments.best_quote: Lucilla made her first bold step out of the limits of Grange Lane for the good of society, and secured at once several important personal advantages, and the great charm of those Thursday evenings which made so entire a revolution in the taste and ideas of Carlingford

assignments.text:
"Papa's bell!" Miss Marjoribanks cried, with a little shriek; and she
got up trembling, and then dropped upon her seat again, and in her
agitated state burst into tears. And Mr Ashburton felt that, under these
most extraordinary circumstances, even so sensible a woman as Lucilla
might be justified in fainting, embarrassing and uncomfortable as that
would be.
assignments.summary: Lucilla recognises the bell as her late father's summons and bursts into tears at the revelation.
assignments.best_quote: "Papa's bell!" Miss Marjoribanks cried, with a little shriek; and she got up trembling, and then dropped upon her seat again, and in her agitated state burst into tears

assignments.text:
She put her hand
upon his arm sharply, and with a certain energy. "Mr Beverley, Thomas is
behind you with the soup," said Miss Marjoribanks. The Archdeacon turned
round to see what it was, conscious that somebody had spoken to him, but
as indifferent to his companion and to civility as he was to Thomas and
the soup. "What?" he said hoarsely, interrupting his scrutiny for the
moment. But when he had met Miss Marjoribanks's eye the Archdeacon sat
down.
assignments.summary: Lucilla firmly redirects the Archdeacon's attention to soup and the servant, bringing him back to social propriety through sheer force of will.
assignments.best_quote: Mr Beverley, Thomas is behind you with the soup

assignments.text:
Lucilla smiled compassionately, and with the gentlest tolerance, at this
wild suggestion. "I was not thinking of Reform," she said, with that
meekness which people assume when it is of no use being impatient. "I
was thinking what your colours were to be. I would not have anything to
do with the old colours, for my part—they would be as bad as opinions,
you know. You may laugh, but I am quite in earnest," said Miss
Marjoribanks.
assignments.summary: Lucilla reveals that the important matter is not Reform but choosing campaign colors (ribbons), which she insists must be new, not the tired old blue and yellow.

assignments.text:
But now, when it was only
Tom—he whom, once upon a time, she had dismissed with affectionate
composure, and given such excellent advice to, and regarded in so
motherly a way—all Lucilla's powers seemed to fail her. It is hard to
have to wind up with such a confession after having so long entertained
a confidence in Lucilla which nothing seemed likely to impair.
assignments.summary: The narrator laments having to confess that Lucilla's emotions have finally been engaged, breaking her previous pattern.
assignments.best_quote: It is hard to have to wind up with such a confession after having so long entertained a confidence in Lucilla which nothing seemed likely to impair.

assignments.text:
Perhaps it
would be false to say that she had suffered in the course of this second
Thursday, or that a superior intelligence like Lucilla's could permit
itself to feel any jealousy of Barbara Lake; but it would be vain to
deny that she had been  surprised . And any one who knows Miss
Marjoribanks will acknowledge that a great deal was implied in that
confession.
assignments.summary: The narrator denies that Lucilla suffered or felt jealousy, but admits she was genuinely surprised by Barbara's behaviour, which carries significant meaning given Lucilla's usual composure.
assignments.best_quote: "Perhaps it would be false to say that she had suffered in the course of this second Thursday, or that a superior intelligence like Lucilla's could permit itself to feel any jealousy of Barbara Lake; but it would be vain to deny that she had been surprised."

assignments.text:
She had been making an effort over herself, and she had
come out of it triumphant; after reading so many good books, it is not
to be wondered at if she felt herself a changed and softened and
elevated character. She had the means in her hands of doing her
candidate's rival a deadly mischief, and yet, for old friendship's sake,
Lucilla made up her mind to forbear.
assignments.summary: Lucilla, having elevated herself through moral reading, possesses the power to damage Cavendish but chooses to forbear for old friendship's sake.
assignments.best_quote: She had been making an effort over herself, and she had come out of it triumphant; after reading so many good books, it is not to be wondered at if she felt herself a changed and softened and elevated character. assignments.text:
When he raised his
head and looked round him, naturally Mr Beverley's eyes went direct to
the mark like an arrow; he looked, and he saw at the centre of the
table, surrounded by every kind of regard and consideration, full in the
light of the lamp, his favourite adventurer, the impostor whom he had
denounced the first time he took his place by Miss Marjoribanks's side.
assignments.summary: The Archdeacon's eyes are drawn directly to Mr Cavendish, exposed fully in the lamp's light at the table's centre—the moment of revelation.
assignments.best_quote: he looked, and he saw at the centre of the table, surrounded by every kind of regard and consideration, full in the light of the lamp, his favourite adventurer, the impostor whom he had denounced

assignments.text:
They were both looking a little black, though the gloom was
moderate in Mr Ashburton's case; but as for Lucilla, she stood between
them a picture of angelic sweetness and goodness, giving a certain
measure of her sympathy to both—Woman the Reconciler, by the side of
those other characters of Inspirer and Consoler, of which the world has
heard. The two inferior creatures scowled with politeness at each other,
but Miss Marjoribanks smiled upon them both.
assignments.summary: The narrator depicts Lucilla as the embodiment of feminine reconciliation, standing between two scowling men as the 'picture of angelic sweetness.'
assignments.best_quote: she stood between them a picture of angelic sweetness and goodness, giving a certain measure of her sympathy to both—Woman the Reconciler, by the side of those other characters of Inspirer and Consoler, of which the world has heard.

assignments.text:

"but she is at home, you know, and I want so much to talk to you. Barbara, good-night; I want Mr Cavendish to walk home with me. Rose,
don't stand in the garden and catch cold; thank you, dear, for such a
pleasant evening," said Lucilla, pressing another kiss upon her little
friend's unwilling cheek.
assignments.summary: Lucilla smoothly separates Cavendish from Barbara, announcing she wishes to walk with him while coolly dismissing Barbara and thanking Rose.

assignments.text:
What was he to do? He could not publicly expose the man
who had just received this mark of confidence from his young hostess,
who knew everything. Perhaps it was one of the greatest trials of
Christian patience and fortitude which the Archdeacon, who was not
great, as he himself would have said, in the passive virtues, had
undergone in all the course of his life.
assignments.summary: The Archdeacon faces a terrible choice: expose Cavendish and shame Lucilla, or remain silent against his duty.
assignments.best_quote: Perhaps it was one of the greatest trials of Christian patience and fortitude which the Archdeacon, who was not great, as he himself would have said, in the passive virtues, had undergone in all the course of his life

assignments.text:
Up to this
time she had managed everything herself, which was comparatively easy;
but she felt by instinct that now was the moment to make a high effort
and leave things alone. And it may be added that nothing but an inherent
sense of doing the right thing under the circumstances could have
inspired Miss Marjoribanks to the crowning achievement of keeping out of
the way.
assignments.summary: Lucilla recognizes that her usual direct management would be wrong; instead, she must deliberately refrain from intervening—a higher achievement of control through non-action.
assignments.best_quote: she felt by instinct that now was the moment to make a high effort and leave things alone

assignments.text:
"Oh, yes," said Lucilla, softening into a smile. "Perfectly, I assure
you. He is one of papa's guests, and very much respected in Carlingford;
and he is one of my—very particular friends," Miss Marjoribanks added. She laughed as she spoke, a kind of laugh which is only appropriate to
one subject, and which is as good, any day, as a confession; and the
flush was so obliging as to return at that moment to her ingenuous
countenance.
assignments.summary: Lucilla reveals through suggestive language, laughter, and the return of her blush that Mr Cavendish is more than a friend.
assignments.best_quote: He is one of papa's guests, and very much respected in Carlingford; and he is one of my—very particular friends

assignments.text:
That was what he came to, poor
man! after all his experiences; a man who was capable of so much better
things—a man even who, if he had made a right use of his opportunities,
might once have had as good a chance as any other of marrying Lucilla
herself. If there ever was an instance of chances thrown away and lost
opportunities, surely here was that lamentable example.
assignments.summary: The narrator laments that Mr Cavendish might have won Lucilla had he used his opportunities wisely; he exemplifies thrown-away chances.
assignments.best_quote: a man who was capable of so much better things—a man even who, if he had made a right use of his opportunities, might once have had as good a chance as any other of marrying Lucilla herself

assignments.text:
It was a revelation which took the town perfectly by storm, and startled
everybody out of their senses. Lucilla's plans, which she thought so
wicked, went out all of a sudden, in a certain dull amaze and dismay, to
which no words could give any expression. Such was the second
inconceivable reverse of fortune which happened to Miss Marjoribanks,
more unexpected, more incomprehensible still than the other, in the very
midst of her most important activities and hopes.
assignments.summary: Lucilla's carefully suppressed hopes for her future are instantly extinguished by the revelation of her father's financial ruin, which is even more incomprehensible than his death.
assignments.best_quote: Lucilla's plans, which she thought so wicked, went out all of a sudden, in a certain dull amaze and dismay, to which no words could give any expression

assignments.text:
"The enlightened electors of Carlingford do not demand,
like other less educated constituencies, a system of political doctrines
cut and dry, or a representative bound to give up his own judgment, and
act according to arbitrary promises," said the daring candidate: "what
they want is an honest man, resolved to do his duty by his country, his
borough, and his constituency; and it is this idea alone which has
induced me to solicit your suffrages." This was what Mr Ashburton said
in his address, though at that moment he had still his other address in
his pocket, in which he had entered at some length into his distinctive
personal views.
assignments.summary: Mr Ashburton's published address appeals to Carlingford's vanity as an 'enlightened' electorate needing only 'an honest man,' flattering them while avoiding specific political commitments.
assignments.best_quote: The enlightened electors of Carlingford do not demand, like other less educated constituencies, a system of political doctrines cut and dry, or a representative bound to give up his own judgment, and act according to arbitrary promises, said the daring candidate: what they want is an honest man, resolved to do his duty by his country, his borough, and his constituency; and it is this idea alone which has induced me to solicit your suffrages.

assignments.text:
And Lucilla certainly was not herself for
the first half-hour. She kept close to the door, and regarded the
staircase with an anxious countenance. When she was herself at the helm
of affairs, there was a certain security that everything would go on
tolerably—but nobody could tell what a set of men left to themselves
might or might not do. This was the most dreadful moment of the evening.
assignments.summary: Lucilla's composure cracks in the drawing-room; she anxiously awaits the men, fearing uncontrolled conversation.
assignments.best_quote: When she was herself at the helm of affairs, there was a certain security that everything would go on tolerably—but nobody could tell what a set of men left to themselves might or might not do

assignments.text:
I am
going away too," said Mr Beverley; and he stopped short, and resisted
the effort his prisoner made to withdraw. Oddly enough at that moment
his Rectory rose suddenly before him as in a vision—his Rectory, all
handsome and sombre, without a soul in it, room after room uninhabited,

assignments.summary: The Archdeacon envisions his empty, handsome Rectory and its profound loneliness, contrasting it with the garden and cottage that suddenly seem desirable.
assignments.best_quote: his Rectory rose suddenly before him as in a vision—his Rectory, all handsome and sombre, without a soul in it, room after room uninhabited, and not a sound to be heard, except that of his own foot or his servant's

assignments.text:
And
it was thus, with Miss Marjoribanks leaning on his arm, and General
Travers, in all the warmth of renewed friendship, guarding him on the
other side, that Mr Cavendish, whose head was in a whirl of excitement,
and who did not know what he was doing, was led back in triumph past
Colonel Chiley's very door, where the Archdeacon was lying in wait to
crunch his bones, back from all his aberrations into the very heart of
Grange Lane.
assignments.summary: Cavendish is led in triumph by Lucilla and General Travers past the Archdeacon's position and back to Grange Lane, fully restored under Lucilla's influence.
assignments.best_quote: And it was thus, with Miss Marjoribanks leaning on his arm, and General Travers, in all the warmth of renewed friendship, guarding him on the other side, that Mr Cavendish, whose head was in a whirl of excitement, and who did not know what he was doing, was led back in triumph past Colonel Chiley's very door, where the Archdeacon was lying in wait to crunch his bones, back from all his aberrations into the very heart of Grange Lane.

assignments.text:
There are people who talk of
themselves, and think of themselves, as it were, under protest, and with
depreciation, not actually able to convince themselves that anybody
cares; but Lucilla, for her part, had the calmest and most profound
conviction that, when she discussed her own doings and plans and
clevernesses, she was bringing forward the subject most interesting to
her audience as well as to herself. Such a conviction is never without
its fruits.
assignments.summary: Lucilla's complete conviction in her own importance is the source of her persuasiveness; she genuinely believes her interests are everyone's interests.
assignments.best_quote: Lucilla, for her part, had the calmest and most profound conviction that, when she discussed her own doings and plans and clevernesses, she was bringing forward the subject most interesting to her audience as well as to herself

assignments.text:
It was at this moment that Lucilla turned round radiant upon the
observant assembly. The change occurred in less than a moment, so

Marjoribanks turned round upon the company and took Mr Cavendish's arm,

assignments.summary: Lucilla's anxiety vanishes the instant the men arrive; she radiant and claims Cavendish's arm before the assembled company.
assignments.best_quote: The change occurred in less than a moment, so suddenly that nobody saw the actual point of revolution

assignments.text:

saw him. I am sure I am very glad for one thing. He can't be married or
dead, as people used to say.
assignments.summary: Lucilla graciously thanks her father and notes that foreknowledge of the return is preferable to a surprise encounter.
assignments.best_quote: It would have been a great deal worse if I had not known of it before I saw him.

assignments.text:
"Tell me, for Heaven's sake, what you mean!" cried the Archdeacon. "You
do not think, surely, that I for a moment meant to imply that Helen
would waste a thought upon such a miscreant. Good Heavens, marry him! You must be raving. She would as soon think of—going for a soldier,"
said Mr Beverley, with a hoarse and perfectly unmirthful laugh, "or
doing anything else that was mad and unnatural.
assignments.summary: The Archdeacon vehemently denies that Mrs Mortimer could ever consider marrying Kavan, responding with shocked laughter and hyperbolic comparisons.
assignments.best_quote: Good Heavens, marry him! You must be raving. She would as soon think of—going for a soldier, said Mr Beverley, with a hoarse and perfectly unmirthful laugh, or doing anything else that was mad and unnatural.

assignments.text:
"If you were to read it to me," said Miss Marjoribanks, "I should be
sure to be convinced that you were quite right, and to go in with you

assignments.summary: Lucilla refuses to hear his address, arguing that if convinced of his views, she would be useless as a unifying force among divided committee members.

If it were to drive papa and Sir John and the Colonel all to their own ways of thinking, we never should make any progress. I would never mind about anybody's ways of thinking, if I were you.

assignments.text:
The Archdeacon rose to his feet in the excitement of the discovery; he
put his hand over his eyes as if to clear them. He said, "Good God!"
loud out, with an accent of horror which paralysed the two people lower
down than himself. As for Miss Marjoribanks, she was not paralysed—she
who had not lost a single glance of his eyes or movement of his large
person. Lucilla rose to the height of the position.
assignments.summary: The Archdeacon rises in shock, exclaiming 'Good God!' with horror; Lucilla remains unflustered and attentive to his every reaction.
assignments.best_quote: Good God!

assignments.text:
He did
not even give his daughter that credit for sincerity which she deserved,
but set it all to the score of her genius, which was complimentary,
certainly, in one point of view; but the fact was that Lucilla was
perfectly sincere, and that she did what was natural to her under
guidance of her genius, so as always to be in good fortune, just as Tom
Marjoribanks, under the guidance of his, brought discredit even upon
those eternal ordinances of English government which fixed the time of
the Carlingford assizes.
assignments.summary: The narrator clarifies that Lucilla is genuinely sincere in her calculations, acting naturally according to her nature, unlike Tom whose nature brings chaos.
assignments.best_quote: the fact was that Lucilla was perfectly sincere, and that she did what was natural to her under guidance of her genius, so as always to be in good fortune, just as Tom Marjoribanks, under the guidance of his, brought discredit even upon those eternal ordinances of English government which fixed the time of the Carlingford assizes.

assignments.text:
"Yes, I am going to see Miss Marjoribanks," he said, with a face
which extremity rendered stolid and impassible. As for poor Barbara, her
colour changed in a moment. The very least that she had a right to
expect was that he should have asked her pardon, put himself at her
feet; and her mingled spite and humiliation and mortification at this
response were beyond telling.
assignments.summary: Mr Cavendish admits his intention to visit Lucilla, shocking Barbara into an emotional transformation from manipulative to devastated.
assignments.best_quote: Yes, I am going to see Miss Marjoribanks

assignments.text:
"Yes," said Miss Marjoribanks, with a certain solemnity, interrupting
him; "I have been thinking a great deal—and  hearing  a great deal
about you, Mr Cavendish." When she had said this Lucilla sighed, and her
sigh found a terrible echo in her hearer's bosom. She knew that he
turned green in the darkness as he gave an anxious look at her. But he
was too much alarmed to give her an opportunity of studying his face.
assignments.summary: Lucilla announces she has heard much about Cavendish, causing him visible distress which she observes keenly.
assignments.best_quote: "Yes," said Miss Marjoribanks, with a certain solemnity, interrupting him; "I have been thinking a great deal—and hearing a great deal about you, Mr Cavendish." When she had said this Lucilla sighed, and her sigh found a terrible echo in her hearer's bosom. She knew that he turned green in the darkness as he gave an anxious look at her.

assignments.text:
If some cruel
spectator had thrown into the fire that Brussels veil with which her
imagination had so long played, and Barbara had stood heart-struck,
watching the filmy tissue dissolve into ashes before her eyes, her sense
of sudden anguish could not have been more acute.
assignments.summary: Barbara's anguish is compared to watching her imagined Brussels wedding veil burn to ashes.
assignments.best_quote: If some cruel spectator had thrown into the fire that Brussels veil with which her imagination had so long played, and Barbara had stood heart-struck, watching the filmy tissue dissolve into ashes before her eyes, her sense of sudden anguish could not have been more acute.

assignments.text:
She went
down to the door, all palpitating with renewed hope, and, at the same
time, with the dread that he might escape her in the moment which was
necessary for her passage downstairs. But when she opened the door and
appeared with her cheeks glowing, and her eyes blazing, and her heart
thumping in her breast, in the midst of that quiet twilight, the object
of her hopes was still there.
assignments.summary: Barbara comes down and appears at the door, her cheeks glowing and eyes blazing, eager to hold Mr Cavendish before he can escape.
assignments.best_quote: when she opened the door and appeared with her cheeks glowing, and her eyes blazing, and her heart thumping in her breast

assignments.text:
"Lucilla," said Aunt Jemima solemnly, "you think you have a great deal
of courage, and now is your time to show it. He has left you without a
farthing—he that was always thought to be so rich. It is quite true
what I am saying. He has gone and died and left nothing, Lucilla.
assignments.summary: Aunt Jemima solemnly announces that Dr Marjoribanks has left Lucilla penniless, having lost all his fortune.
assignments.best_quote: He has left you without a farthing—he that was always thought to be so rich. It is quite true what I am saying. He has gone and died and left nothing, Lucilla.

assignments.text:
"I want to know who Mr Kavan is?" said Miss Marjoribanks, much startled. She had for the moment forgotten the Archdeacon's discovery and her own
suspicions; and the idea of connecting the man who had (apparently) fled
from Mr Beverley's presence, with the innocent and helpless woman upon
whom the appearance of the Broad Churchman had so overwhelming an
effect, had never hitherto entered her imagination.
assignments.summary: Lucilla's shock at the name Kavan suddenly reconnects her earlier observations and brings the entire mystery into focus.
assignments.best_quote: I want to know who Mr Kavan is? said Miss Marjoribanks, much startled. She had for the moment forgotten the Archdeacon's discovery and her own suspicions; and the idea of connecting the man who had (apparently) fled from Mr Beverley's presence, with the innocent and helpless woman upon whom the appearance of the Broad Churchman had so overwhelming an effect, had never hitherto entered her imagination.

assignments.text:
This was the dread that
overshadowed the mind of Lucilla as she composed herself to rest after
her fatigues. When she slept the sleep of the innocent, it still pursued
her into her dreams.
assignments.summary: Lucilla's dread about the luncheon incident continues to haunt her even as she falls asleep.

assignments.text:
She felt that the moment had arrived
for a trial of her courage very different from the exertions which had
hitherto sufficed her. Nothing but the most solemn intentions could have
supported the Rector in that severe pose of his figure and features,
every line in which revealed an intention of being "faithful"; and the
accompanying mute in black, whose office the culprit could not divine,
had a veil over her face, and wore a widow's dress.
assignments.summary: Mr Bury's rigid posture and the widow's black attire and veil suggest he arrives on a grave mission of Christian duty.

assignments.text:
But this clandestine inspection met with the
failure it deserved, for there was no light in the room except the
moonlight, which made three white blotches on the carpet where the
windows were, burying everything else in the profoundest darkness; and
the spy knocked his foot against something which reduced him to sudden
and well-merited agony. As for Mrs Chiley, she was discretion itself,
and would say nothing even to her niece.
assignments.summary: Mr Cavendish's clandestine inspection of the dark drawing-room ends when he trips painfully on furniture; Mrs Chiley remains discretely silent about what she saw.
assignments.best_quote: the spy knocked his foot against something which reduced him to sudden and well-merited agony

assignments.text:
Perhaps a man who has always been used to be recognised as one of
the members of a local aristocracy, would not have seen anything half so
precious as Mr Cavendish saw in the fact of being everywhere known and
acknowledged as a constituent part of Grange Lane;—recognised by the
county people, and by the poor people, and pointed out as he passed by
one and another to any stranger who might happen to be so ignorant as
not to know Mr Cavendish.
assignments.summary: The narrator explains that Cavendish, unused to social prominence, treasures his recognition in Carlingford more deeply than those born to such status would.
assignments.best_quote: Perhaps a man who has always been used to be recognised as one of the members of a local aristocracy, would not have seen anything half so precious as Mr Cavendish saw in the fact of being everywhere known and acknowledged as a constituent part of Grange Lane

assignments.text:
The old disused bell that had so often called Dr
Marjoribanks up at night, and which hung near the door of the old
Doctor's room, just over the drawing-room, began to peal through the
silence, as if rung by a hand too impatient to notice what it was with
which it made its summons.
assignments.summary: The long-disused bell of Lucilla's late father summons from above, pealing urgently as if rung by an impatient hand.
assignments.best_quote: The old disused bell that had so often called Dr Marjoribanks up at night, and which hung near the door of the old Doctor's room, just over the drawing-room, began to peal through the silence, as if rung by a hand too impatient to notice what it was with which it made its summons

assignments.text:
He was dead, and he had made an elaborate will, which was all as just
and righteous as a will could be; but after the will was read, it was
found out that everything named in it had disappeared like a bubble. Instead of being the richest, Dr Marjoribanks was one of the poorest
men in Carlingford when he shut his door behind him on that snowy night.
assignments.summary: The Doctor's will is just, but upon reading it, everything named has vanished. The Doctor was actually one of the poorest men in Carlingford.
assignments.best_quote: after the will was read, it was found out that everything named in it had disappeared like a bubble. Instead of being the richest, Dr Marjoribanks was one of the poorest men in Carlingford when he shut his door behind him on that snowy night

assignments.text:
For the first time in her life she not
only did not know what she would do, but she did not know what she
wanted to do. There could now be no mistaking what Mr Ashburton's
intentions were. Up to a very recent time Lucilla had been able to take
refuge in her mourning, and conclude that she had no present occasion to
disturb herself. But now that calm was over.
assignments.summary: Lucilla recognises that Mr Ashburton intends a proposal and faces an unprecedented crisis of indecision about her true desires.
assignments.best_quote: For the first time in her life she not only did not know what she would do, but she did not know what she wanted to do

assignments.text:
Lucilla uttered a scream of genuine alarm and dismay; and then she came
to herself, and saw the force of her position. She had it in her power
to turn the tables on the Rector, and she did not hesitate, as a weaker
woman might have done, out of consideration for anybody's feelings.
assignments.summary: Lucilla gasps in alarm at Mr Bury's suggestion, then quickly recognizes the opportunity to turn the tables on him.

assignments.text:
"Do
you mean you have found some one for him to marry?" she asked, with a
look of artless surprise, bending her earnest gaze on Mr Bury's face.
assignments.summary: Lucilla feigns artless misunderstanding, asking if Mr Bury has found a remarriage prospect for her father.
assignments.best_quote: Do you mean you have found some one for him to marry?

assignments.text:
You may think the liberty is pleasant at first, but if you
had a Christian friend to watch over and take care of you——What is the
matter?" said the Rector, in great alarm. It was only that the poor
widow who was to have charge of Lucilla, according to his benevolent
intention, looked so like fainting, that Miss Marjoribanks jumped up
from her chair and rang the bell hastily.
assignments.summary: As Mr Bury outlines his plan, Mrs Mortimer looks ready to faint, forcing Lucilla to ring the bell and intervene with practical concern.

assignments.text:
It was not Lucilla's way to
lose time about anything; she took the poor woman by the shoulders and
all but lifted her to the sofa, where she was lying down with her bonnet
off when the Rector came to his senses. To describe the feelings with
which Mr Bury contemplated this little  entr'acte , which was not in his
programme, would be beyond our powers.
assignments.summary: Lucilla efficiently takes charge, helping the fainting Mrs Mortimer to the sofa while the Rector watches helplessly, unable to proceed with his address.

assignments.text:
When he was gone Miss Marjoribanks felt the full importance of
her victory; and then, though she had not hesitated to sacrifice this
poor woman when it was necessary to have a victim, that moment was over,
and she had no pleasure in being cruel; on the contrary, she went and
sat by her patient, and talked, and was very kind to her; and after a
while heard all her story, and was more comforting than the Rector could
have been for his life.
assignments.summary: Once her victory is assured, Lucilla abandons her calculated coldness and becomes genuinely kind to the suffering Mrs Mortimer, sitting with her and offering comfort.

assignments.text:
"Lucilla," cried the unlucky fellow, "is it possible that you really
have misunderstood me all this time? Do you mean to say that you don't
know? Oh, Lucilla, listen just five minutes. It isn't because I am your
cousin. I wish to Heaven I was not your cousin, but some one you had
never seen before. I mean I want you to consent to—to—to—marry me,
Lucilla. That is what I mean.
assignments.summary: Tom finally explicitly proposes marriage, admitting his long-held love and his wish that he were not her cousin, begging Lucilla to listen to him.
assignments.best_quote: I mean I want you to consent to—to—to—marry me, Lucilla.

assignments.text:
It was when she was in this unhappy humour
that her eye fell upon Mr Cavendish, who was in the act of making the
appeal to Lucilla which we have already recorded. Barbara had never as
yet had a lover, but she had read an unlimited number of novels, which
came to nearly the same thing, and she saw at a glance that this was
somebody who resembled the indispensable hero.
assignments.summary: Barbara spots Mr Cavendish and, inspired by novel heroines, recognises him as the archetypal hero; she imagines how the humble heroine often wins him over rivals.
assignments.best_quote: Barbara had never as yet had a lover, but she had read an unlimited number of novels, which came to nearly the same thing

assignments.text:
But this
evening there could be no mistake about it. The words were arrested on
the very lips of the talkers; Mrs Woodburn paused in the midst of doing
Lucilla, and, as we have before said, Mr Cavendish broke a flirtation
clean off at its most interesting moment.
assignments.summary: The duet shocks the assembly into complete silence: conversations freeze, Mrs Woodburn ceases her mimicry, Cavendish abandons his flirtation—an unmissable moment.
assignments.best_quote: The words were arrested on the very lips of the talkers; Mrs Woodburn paused in the midst of doing Lucilla, and, as we have before said, Mr Cavendish broke a flirtation clean off at its most interesting moment.

assignments.text:
"It was a great deal more than pleasant," said Mr Cavendish; "and as for
your conception of social politics, it is masterly," the future M.P.
added, in a tone which struck Lucilla as very significant; not that she
cared particularly about Mr Cavendish's meaning, but still, when a young
man who intends to go into Parliament congratulates a young lady upon
her statesmanlike views, and her conception of politics, it must be
confessed that it looks a little particular; and then, if that was what
he meant, it was no doubt Lucilla's duty to make up her mind.
assignments.summary: Mr Cavendish congratulates Lucilla on her statesmanlike views with a tone that suggests romantic interest, prompting Lucilla to recognize this may require her decision.
assignments.best_quote: your conception of social politics, it is masterly

assignments.text:
"I shall be quite interested to watch  you , Lucilla, when it
comes to be your turn, and see how you manage," she went on, with a keen
look at Miss Marjoribanks; and Mr Cavendish laughed. He too looked at
her, and Lucilla felt herself in rather a delicate position: not that
she was agitated, as might have been the case had the future M.P. for
Carlingford "engaged her affections," as she herself would have said.
assignments.summary: Mrs Woodburn makes a pointed observation about how Lucilla will handle her own marriage, implying awareness of Mr Cavendish's interest and placing Lucilla in a delicate position.
assignments.best_quote: I shall be quite interested to watch you, Lucilla, when it comes to be your turn, and see how you manage

assignments.text:
It was not that she was unduly flattered by Mr
Cavendish's attentions, as might have happened to an inexperienced young
woman; for Lucilla, with her attractions and genius, had not reached the
mature age of nineteen without receiving the natural homage of mankind
on several clearly-defined occasions. But then the present case had
various features peculiar to itself, which prevented Lucilla from
crushing it in the bud, as she had meant to do with her cousin's
ill-fated passion.
assignments.summary: The narrator reveals that Lucilla, experienced in receiving male attention, recognizes Mr Cavendish's case as different because of political considerations distinct from her cousin Tom's situation.

assignments.text:
The unfortunate Tom grew red and then he grew green under this question
and that awful look. "No, Miss Bury, I can't say I do," he answered
humbly; and the amusing man was so much less brotherly than Tom that he
burst into unsympathetic laughter. As for Lucilla, it was the first real
check she had sustained in the beginning of her career.
assignments.summary: Tom is mortified by Miss Bury's question and admits he does not believe in Jove; the barrister laughs unkindly, and Lucilla faces her first real check.
assignments.best_quote: The unfortunate Tom grew red and then he grew green under this question and that awful look.

assignments.text:
There could not
have been a more unfortunate  contretemps , and there is no telling how
disastrous the effect might have been, had not her courage and
coolness, not to say her orthodoxy, been equal to the occasion. She gave
her cousin a look which was still more terrible than Miss Bury's, and
then she took affairs into her own hands.
assignments.summary: The narrator emphasizes that a damaging social disaster has occurred, but Lucilla's courage, coolness, and orthodoxy allow her to take control and repair the situation.
assignments.best_quote: There could not have been a more unfortunate contretemps, and there is no telling how disastrous the effect might have been, had not her courage and coolness, not to say her orthodoxy, been equal to the occasion.

assignments.text:
She dreamed that she stood at the altar by the side
of the member for Carlingford, and that Mr Bury, with inflexible
cruelty, insisted upon marrying her to Tom Marjoribanks instead; and
then the scene changed, and instead of receiving the salutations of Mr
Cavendish as M.P. for the borough, it was the amusing man, in the
character of the defeated candidate, who grinned and nodded at her, and
said from the hustings that he would never forget the luncheon that had
been his first introduction to Carlingford.
assignments.summary: Lucilla dreams of being forced to marry Tom instead of securing Mr Cavendish as M.P., and of public mockery about the luncheon incident.
